# Using the S&P 500 page: my answer as a 61-year-old saver

## 1. What I would do, and how sure I am

The page never asked who I am. I kept its example numbers: **10,000 ₪ now ("סכום היום"), then 500 ₪ a month ("הפקדה חודשית"), for 10 years ("שנים"), assuming 7% a year ("תשואה בשנה")**.

**Where to hold the money:** a securities account at **פסגות** (Psagot). Every list on the page puts it first. Psagot charges about **1,057 ₪** over the 10 years, while the banks charge 4,500 to 10,600 ₪ and the cheap-sounding online brokers charge more than 23,000 ₪. I'm fairly sure about this part, because a gap of about 5,000 ₪ over my own bank is real money. I also noticed "קיבלתם מחיר אחר? הזינו אותו", which tells me prices can be bargained. So I'd phone my own bank first and ask them to match.

**Which fund:** the page's pick is **"ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)", number 5139282**. Its fees read "דמי ניהול: 0% קבועים, 0% משתנים, 0.02% נאמן", which looks almost free. The runner-up, **"אלטשולר שחם מחקה S&P 500 (4D)" 5139100**, would leave me only **43 ₪** less ("−43 ₪ לעומת הבחירה שלכם"). I'm less sure about the fund than the account. Both of those funds say **"שנה אחת"**, so they have only one year of history. **"קסם KTF S&P 500 (4D)"** has "4 שנים" of history and costs me 447 ₪ more over ten years. As a careful person I might pay 447 ₪ for a longer record, so I'm torn between Yelin and Kesem.

**How much I'd end up with:** about **86,500 ₪** ("86,492 ₪") from **70,000 ₪** put in. The page says this is "בכסף של היום, אחרי דמי ניהול ומס", meaning in today's money, after fees and tax. Two big conditions are written under it: **"אם הדולר לא זז מול השקל"**, which means only if the dollar stays level with the shekel, and the 7% is just a guess. The bottom of the page says plainly **"תשואה לדוגמה, לא תחזית"**, an example, not a forecast. So I'd treat it as "somewhere around 86,000, could be a lot more or a lot less."

I'm fairly sure about Psagot, only half sure about the fund, and I don't trust the final amount much, because the dollar alone moved between −12.5% and +13.4% in a single year.

## 2. The parts I actually used

- The top: the title **"איפה ואיך הכי זול להשקיע במדד, לאורך זמן"**, the **S&P 500** button, and the four boxes with sliders.
- The result box: **"הפקדתם 70,000 ₪"**, **"הבחירה שלכם · הזול 86,492 ₪"** and **"הזוג הבא בתור 86,449 ₪"**.
- The account list **"כל החשבונות"** on the right.
- The fund list **"כל הקרנות על מדד S&P 500"** on the left, mainly the top few rows.
- The section **"עם נטרול מט״ח או בלי: מה קרה בפועל"**, especially its bold **"השורה התחתונה"** (bottom line).
- The table at the very end, **"עכשיו: ... ירושלים. נשארים בסוף 79,176 ₪"**, because it showed me how a bank fares compared with Psagot.

## 3. Block by block, top to bottom

- **Top menu (מקור, מדריך, חברות ומסלולים, השקעה במדד, חוקים וכללים):** Skipped. I was already on the right page.
- **Title and subtitle:** Used. "בוחרים חשבון ניירות ערך וקרן, ורואים כמה יישאר לכם" (pick an account and a fund, see what's left) told me exactly what the page does. Good.
- **Index buttons (MSCI World, נאסד״ק 100, S&P 500, ת״א-125...):** Used only to check that S&P 500 was selected. "האתר לא ממליץ על מדד" (the site doesn't recommend an index) was fine with me.
- **"מדד S&P 500" description:** Read it. "הכסף מושקע בדולרים" made me realise there's a dollar risk. "אפשר להחזיק אותו גם דרך קרן חוץ" means it can also be held through a foreign fund, which I didn't follow up yet.
- **Four boxes with sliders:** Used them, but kept the defaults.
- **"אינפלציה" button and the line "בכסף של היום · שער הדולר 3.17 ₪...":** Skimmed. I gather the amounts are already adjusted for prices rising. I didn't press the button, because I wasn't sure what it would change.
- **Result box (70,000 → 86,492 / 86,449):** Used. This is the heart of it.
- **"כמה זה עולה לכם ב־10 שנים, בכל אחד מהזוגות" (coloured bar):** I mostly missed this. My screenshots cut it off; I only saw the coloured legend.
- **"עלות אצלכם, לעומת הזוג הבא" (account 1 ₪ more, fund 58 ₪ less, tax 14 ₪ more):** Skimmed. The point is that the difference is tiny. "14 ₪ יותר מס... כי נשאר לכם יותר רווח" (more tax because you kept more profit) made sense.
- **Psagot card ("מה החשבון גובה ב־10 שנים: 1,057 ₪"):** Used.
- **Yelin fund card:** Used the fees line. Skipped "מנהל הקרן" (the fund manager's name).
- **"סננו לפי תווית" filter buttons (מנוטרל מט״ח, קרן סל, קרן חוץ בת״א...):** Skipped. Too many coloured buttons, and I didn't know what most of them mean.
- **Fund list:** I used the top three or four rows and skimmed the rest. Once I saw minus amounts in the thousands (−3,671, −4,157, −4,492), I stopped reading closely.
- **Foreign funds (iShares, Vanguard...):** Confused me. Every one said **"אין מחיר כאן"** (no price here) and **"עוד לא נאסף"** (not collected yet). So why list them? The note "לא נמצאה אמירה רשמית איך ממסים בישראל קרן אמריקאית" (no official word on how Israel taxes an American fund) scared me off them, and I'm glad it did.
- **Currency-hedged fund (הראל מחקה S&P 500 (4A) - מנוטרלת מט״ח):** Read it. **"בין +2,212 ₪ ל־−23,766 ₪"** depending on the dollar, and "−2.44% בשנה" against the index. That told me to stay away.
- **"למה חלק מהקרנות בלי מחיר בפסגות":** Skimmed. "בתעריפון אין שורה לניירות ערך זרים" means Psagot's price list has no line for foreign securities. OK.
- **Account list (Leumi, Discount, Hapoalim...):** Used the amounts and the small grey numbers. Read the "לא בחישוב" lines, which are prices the calculation leaves out. Most are for "צעירים, חיילים, סטודנטים" (young people, soldiers, students), which isn't me. But at Hapoalim: **"לגמלאים... לנשים מגיל 60 וגברים מגיל 65"**. That one made me stop, because at 61 it might apply to me. The page leaves it out of the calculation, so I don't know what it would mean for my money.
- **Interactive Brokers:** Confused me. "אין נתון", "אין מחיר בשקלים", "אבל לא כתוב שאי אפשר לקנות קרן כזאת". It says there's no data and no shekel price, but nothing says I can't buy the fund there. Then it shows a number (82,842 ₪) anyway. I gave up on it.
- **"מה הכי משנה את מה שיישאר לכם" (chart and table):** Skimmed. The line I took away: **"אם תגדילו כל מספר ב־20%, הכי ישנה מספר השנים: 19,116 ₪ יותר בסוף"**, meaning more years helps most. Useful, but it didn't affect which fund to pick.
- **"עם נטרול מט״ח או בלי: מה קרה בפועל" and the three boxes:** Read the text and **"השורה התחתונה: הנטרול לא מגן מירידה של השוק"** (hedging doesn't protect you when the market falls). That was the clearest sentence on the page for me.
- **The two bar charts and the yearly table (2022–2025):** Skimmed. Too many numbers.
- **"זה בסיס קטן: 4 שנים..." and the sources:** Read the first; it's honest. Skipped the sources.
- **"מתחילים מבחירה אחת, ורואים מה משפר אותה ובכמה" (waterfall chart):** Half-used, half-confused (details in section 4).
- **The "עכשיו: ... ירושלים" tables:** Used the account side. Skimmed the fund side.
- **Notes at the bottom:** Read them. "התשואה שבחישוב: תשואה לדוגמה, לא תחזית" (the return is an example, not a forecast) matters. "האתר לא ממליץ על מדד" was fine.
- **Footer:** Skipped.

## 4. Lists, tables and charts: what I looked at and ignored

- **Account list:** I looked at the account name, the big amount ("נשאר", what's left), and the small dotted grey amount, which I took to be the account cost. I ignored the coloured bar (orange, yellow, red). The legend says "עמלת קנייה ומכירה, דמי משמרת, דמי ניהול חשבון, המרת מטבע" (buying/selling fees, custody fees, account fees, currency conversion). I didn't need to know which colour was which; the total was enough. I ignored the "#" column and the round radio buttons.
- **Fund list:** I looked at the fund name, the number (5139282), the "לעומת הבחירה" column (compared with my choice, e.g. −43 ₪), and the "שנה אחת / 4 שנים" line. I glanced at the "מול המדד" column (against the index: +0.37%, +0.32%) without understanding it. I ignored nearly all the coloured labels (צוברת, עסקת החלף, כמה דרכים יחד...) except **"מס גם על שינוי המטבע"** (tax on currency changes too) and **"מנוטרלת מט״ח"** (currency-hedged), which sounded like they matter.
- **Sensitivity chart:** I read the table, not the chart: the "ההפרש" (difference) column and the "שנים" (years) row. The four lines (yellow years, orange monthly, purple return, turquoise amount today) I only looked at to see which climbs steepest.
- **Dollar and fund bar charts:** I noticed the white bars, +13.4 and −12.5, as the years the dollar jumped. I couldn't tell the turquoise and yellow bars apart well enough to understand them.
- **Yearly table:** Only the "4 השנים יחד" (all four years) row. The hedged fund made +35.9% and the unhedged ones +50.4% to +56.8%. That was enough for me.
- **Waterfall chart:** I followed it: 79,176 now (Jerusalem), then **"+4,972 ₪"** for changing the account, then **"+2,344 ₪"** for changing the fund type, giving 86,492. That part was clear. The table under it confused me, though. The Jerusalem column shows costs (6,432), but the next columns show differences with signs (−5,416, +444). I couldn't tell what was a cost and what was a saving. The legend (grey, turquoise, pink, yellow, and a padlock "נשען על כלל מס פתוח: מוצג ולא מדורג", relies on an open tax rule: shown but not ranked) I ignored.
- **Green/red bars in the "עוד / פחות" tables:** I looked at them. Green means more money, red means less. I didn't need more than that.

## 5. What I didn't understand

- **"(4D)" and "(4A)"** after the fund names. I worked out that 4A is the hedged one, but nothing explains it.
- **"עסקת החלף", "כמה דרכים יחד", "מחזיקה את המניות"**: what's the difference, and should it worry me?
- **"קרן מחקה" versus "קרן סל"**: is one safer than the other?
- **"0.02% נאמן"**: who is the trustee, and is that a fee?
- **"מול המדד +0.37% בשנה"**: did the fund beat the index? How is that even possible for a fund that copies it?
- **"מס גם על שינוי המטבע"**: will I pay tax even when the dollar goes up and the stocks don't?
- **"דמי משמרת"**, "עמלת זו על זו", and "הפס נחתך: הסכום ארוך מהמשתנה".
- Why foreign funds are listed with **"אין מחיר כאן"**.
- The plus and minus signs in the waterfall table.

## 6. What I wanted to know and couldn't find

- **Is my money safe at Psagot?** It isn't a bank. If the company gets into trouble, what happens to my fund?
- **What if I need the money before 10 years**, for health or family? Is there a penalty or extra cost to sell early?
- **The Hapoalim price for pensioners or people over 60.** It's mentioned but left out of the calculation. For someone my age, that might change the answer.
- **How to actually start:** how do I open a Psagot account, and can I set up a standing monthly purchase of 500 ₪?
- **How much tax, in plain words?** I saw the figure "25%" only in passing.
- **What does a bad year mean in shekels?** For example: "if the market falls 20% in year 9, you'd have X." At 71 I won't have time to wait for a recovery.
- **Is this better than putting the money in a pension, a study fund, or an investment policy?** At my age that is the real question.
- **A simple statement of how big the dollar risk is** for the fund I'd actually buy, in shekels, the way the hedged fund got "בין +2,212 ל־−23,766".

## 7. If half the page had to go, what goes first

1. The yearly tables and the two bar charts about the dollar and hedging (keep only the "השורה התחתונה" sentence).
2. The "מה הכי משנה" chart and its table.
3. The foreign funds marked "אין מחיר כאן".
4. The rows of coloured labels on every fund, and the "סננו לפי תווית" filters.
5. The waterfall chart and its confusing table. The account and fund lists already say the same thing.
6. The coloured cost bars in the account list. The total amount is enough.

What must stay: the four input boxes, the result box (70,000 → 86,492), the account list with its "לא בחישוב" notes, the top of the fund list, and the sentence "אם הדולר לא זז מול השקל".
